title: Piano Learning Plan
rules: Slow and correct beats fast and sloppy. Use a metronome and only raise the tempo after three clean repetitions.
Hands separately first, then together. Every new piece, every time.
Move on when a week's goal is met, not when the week ends. Repeating a week is normal.
Record yourself once a week (phone is fine). You will hear problems you can't feel while playing.
On a bad day, 15 minutes of the warm-up and technique blocks beats skipping.

blocks.label: Warm-up
blocks.source: Five-finger patterns or scales, slowly, with metronome

blocks.label: Technique
blocks.source: The week's specific exercise (posture, independence, chords)

blocks.label: Reading
blocks.source: Next 1–2 pages of the method book, sight-read one short new piece

blocks.label: Repertoire
blocks.source: One flowkey song in practice mode: hands separate, slow, then together

blocks.label: Ear and theory
blocks.source: One short theory lesson or ear exercise, then play something for fun

restDay.text: Rest day or free day: play whatever you enjoy, no metronome, no goals.

reviewDay.label: Record + log
reviewDay.text: Record the week's piece on your phone, note one thing to fix, and fill in the progress log.

resources.title: Alfred's Basic Adult All-in-One Course, Book 1
resources.why: Lesson, theory and technique in one book for adult beginners; the “Method book” in the weekly reading block (item 00-5753, 160 pages, lay-flat comb binding).

resources.title: flowkey
resources.why: Courses “Introduction to the Piano” → “Playing With Both Hands” → “Intermediate Piano Playing”, plus scale drills and 8 sight-reading lessons; use Wait Mode and slow tempo.

resources.title: musictheory.net lessons
resources.why: Short animated theory lessons, from staff and clefs to seventh chords. Every lesson named in the plan is in the menu on this page.

resources.title: Pianote: 7 Days To Learning Piano
resources.why: Keyboard, five-finger scale, first chords. The free mini-courses Getting Started, Chord Hacks and Sight-Reading Made Simple are linked from its description.

resources.title: Pianote: guide to reading piano notes
resources.why: A reference to keep open while reading.

resources.title: Minuet in G, BWV Anh. 114 (Petzold) on Musopen
resources.why: 3/4, G major, the standard first classical piece. Long credited to Bach; now attributed to Christian Petzold.

resources.title: Schumann, Album für die Jugend, Op. 68 on IMSLP
resources.why: Public-domain editions plus recordings; No. 1 “Melodie” is the first target.

resources.title: Pianote: Play The Blues In 10 Minutes
resources.why: Chapters for the 12-bar form, boogie pattern, the slide, two riffs and triplet rhythm. Learn one chapter per day.

resources.title: Tim Richards: Improvising Blues Piano (Schott)
resources.why: Assumes about Grade 3, roughly a year of steady practice. Keep it for year 2.

resources.title: jazztutorial.com: Shell Voicings lesson
resources.why: Root + 3rd + 7th voicings, the first jazz left hand.

resources.title: Tim Richards: Beginning Jazz Piano, Part 1 (Schott; MusicGurus video course)
resources.why: The book for the jazz module. His Exploring Jazz Piano vol. 1 suits Grade 4 and above, so it comes later.

phases.title: Foundations
phases.goal: Correct posture and hand shape, find any note on the keyboard instantly, read treble and bass clef in the C position, and play a short piece hands together at a slow tempo.
notes: One video per week in block 5 (playing beats watching): Pianote's 7 Days To Learning Piano in week 1, How To Read Notes in week 3. Keep Pianote's written guide to reading notes open as a reference.

weeks.label: Week 1

warmup.text: Finger numbers 1–5. C five-finger pattern (C–G) in each hand, quarter notes at 60 bpm, with metronome.

technique.text: Posture, bench height, curved fingers. Check them before every block this week.

reading.text: Keyboard geography: groups of 2 and 3 black keys, all white note names. musictheory.net lesson “The Staff, Clefs, and Ledger Lines”.

repertoire.text: flowkey course “Introduction to the Piano”, first lessons.

ear.text: Watch Pianote's 7 Days To Learning Piano (keyboard, five-finger scale, first chords), a chapter at a time. Then play something for fun.

weeks.doneWhen: You can name any white key in under 2 seconds.

weeks.label: Week 2

warmup.text: C five-finger pattern, hands separate, then parallel, at 60 bpm.

technique.text: Legato (smooth) vs staccato (detached) on the C pattern. Alternate one bar of each.

reading.text: Note values: whole, half, quarter; 4/4 time. Method book lessons 1–3.

repertoire.text: “Introduction to the Piano”: right-hand lessons and the first song.

ear.text: musictheory.net lessons “Note Duration” and “Measures and Time Signature”. Clap and count rhythms.

weeks.doneWhen: You clap and count a 4-bar rhythm without stopping.

weeks.label: Week 3

warmup.text: C pattern in contrary motion (hands mirror outward), at 60 bpm.

technique.text: G five-finger pattern (G–D), each hand, then parallel.

reading.text: Bass clef notes in C position. Method book lessons 4–6.

ear.text: Rests: musictheory.net lesson “Rest Duration”. Watch Pianote's How To Read Notes.

weeks.doneWhen: You read single notes in both clefs within C–G.

weeks.label: Week 4

warmup.text: Both five-finger patterns (C and G) at 72 bpm.

technique.text: Simple dynamics on the patterns: piano, then forte, then alternating by bar.

reading.text: Intervals 2nd–5th by sight. Method book lessons 7–9.

repertoire.text: Start flowkey course “Playing With Both Hands”.

ear.text: musictheory.net lesson “Generic Intervals”. Play the intervals you read.

weeks.doneWhen: One piece hands together, no stops, at any tempo.

phases.title: Hands together and chords
phases.goal: Play melody in the right hand over block chords in the left, read beyond the five-finger position, and use the sustain pedal cleanly.
notes: The biggest hurdle here is hand independence. If hands-together stalls, cut the tempo in half and practise just the two bars that fail; never restart from bar 1.
flowkey: finish “Playing With Both Hands”, then the scales and arpeggios drills and the 8 sight-reading lessons.
Theory: musictheory.net “The Major Scale”, “Introduction to Chords”, “Triad Inversion” and “Diatonic Triads”, one per fortnight.
Free courses: Pianote's “Chord Hacks” and “Sight-Reading Made Simple”, linked from the description of the 7 Days video.

weeks.label: Weeks 5–6

warmup.text: C major scale, one octave, hands separate, with metronome.

technique.text: Thumb-under crossing: fingers 1-2-3-1-2-3-4-5 going up, slowly. Stop at the crossing and check the hand stays level.

reading.text: Eighth notes, dotted quarter; key signature of G. Method book continues.

repertoire.text: Easy-level songs with melody + single bass notes. Finish “Playing With Both Hands”.

weeks.doneWhen: Scale at 72 bpm, even and without accents.

weeks.label: Weeks 7–8

warmup.text: C major scale, hands separate, then hands together at a slow tempo.

technique.text: Primary chords in C: C, F, G in root position, left hand, changing on the beat with metronome.

reading.text: Triads: how a major chord is built (root, major 3rd, perfect 5th). Chord symbols. Method book continues.

repertoire.text: Songs where the left hand plays chords.

ear.text: musictheory.net lesson “Introduction to Chords”. Pianote's free “Chord Hacks” course.

weeks.doneWhen: You switch C–F–G–C at 80 bpm without looking.

weeks.label: Weeks 9–10

warmup.text: G major scale, one octave, hands separate (mind the F♯).

technique.text: Chords in G: G, C, D, left hand, changing on the beat.

reading.text: Minor triads; the relative minor (A minor). Method book continues.

repertoire.text: Start flowkey course “Intermediate Piano Playing” (fingering, sharps and flats).

ear.text: musictheory.net lesson “Triad Inversion”. Harmonise a simple melody with I–IV–V by ear.

weeks.doneWhen: You harmonise a simple melody with I–IV–V.

weeks.label: Weeks 11–12

warmup.text: C and G major scales, hands together, slowly.

technique.text: Pedal: legato pedalling. Lift and press right after each chord change, listening for the gap or the smear.

reading.text: Sight-read one new 8-bar piece per day, never stopping for mistakes. flowkey's 8 sight-reading lessons.

repertoire.text: One full song you love, polished, with pedal.

ear.text: musictheory.net lesson “Diatonic Triads”. Pianote's free “Sight-Reading Made Simple”.

weeks.doneWhen: A recorded piece you'd play for someone.

phases.title: Real music
phases.goal: Play from a lead sheet (melody + chord symbols), accompany a song with a left-hand pattern, and finish two pieces from the classical beginner repertoire.
notes: Theory for this phase: musictheory.net “Key Signatures”, “Seventh Chords” and “Roman Numeral Analysis: Triads”.
At month 6, decide the next direction (classical, blues, jazz, pop accompaniment) and ask for a new plan. Month 5's seventh chords are placed so that blues or jazz can branch off cleanly from there.

weeks.label: Month 4

warmup.text: Scales C, G, D, F, two octaves, hands together.

technique.text: Chord inversions of C, F, G. Move between them with the hand barely leaving the keys.

reading.text: Reading a lead sheet (melody + chord symbols). Method book continues.

repertoire.text: Bach/Petzold “Minuet in G”: start, hands separate. Plus a flowkey song of choice.

ear.text: The circle of fifths. musictheory.net lesson “Key Signatures”.

weeks.doneWhen: You play I–IV–V with inversions, hand barely moving.

weeks.label: Month 5

warmup.text: Arpeggios C and G, hands separate.

technique.text: Left-hand accompaniment patterns: broken chord, then Alberti bass, over I–IV–V.

reading.text: Minuet in G from the score, hands together in sections.

repertoire.text: Finish Minuet in G. A pop song from a lead sheet with your own accompaniment.

ear.text: Seventh chords (maj7, dom7, m7), the bridge to blues and jazz. musictheory.net lesson “Seventh Chords”.

weeks.doneWhen: You accompany a melody from chord symbols alone.

weeks.label: Month 6

warmup.text: Minor scales: A natural and A harmonic, hands separate, then together.

technique.text: A minor chords; the ii–V–I progression in C (Dm–G–C) in the left hand.

reading.text: Schumann “Melody” (Album for the Young, No. 1) from the score.

repertoire.text: A second classical piece: Schumann's “Melody”. Review and re-record the pieces of the year.

ear.text: Simple transposition: play a known melody in G. musictheory.net lesson “Roman Numeral Analysis: Triads”.

weeks.doneWhen: Two recorded pieces + one self-arranged song.

modules.title: Blues
modules.intro: A good detour from week 9 onward, once you have I–IV–V chords. Before that it mostly produces frustration. Swaps into the technique and repertoire blocks; warm-up, reading and theory follow the main plan.

technique.text: 12-bar blues in C with a left-hand boogie pattern, slowly, with metronome.

repertoire.text: Pianote's Play The Blues In 10 Minutes, one chapter per day: the 12-bar form, the boogie pattern, the slide.

weeks.doneWhen: You play the 12-bar form in C with the boogie pattern without stopping.

technique.text: Dominant 7th chords C7, F7, G7 over the 12-bar form. Swing / triplet feel on the boogie pattern.

repertoire.text: Chapters: the two riffs and the triplet rhythm. Put one riff over the form.

weeks.doneWhen: 12-bar blues with C7–F7–G7 in a swing feel, at a steady tempo.

technique.text: The blues scale in C (C, E♭, F, F♯, G, B♭), up and down, then over the boogie pattern.

repertoire.text: Improvise with the riffs and the blues scale over the 12-bar form. Record one chorus.

weeks.doneWhen: A recorded 12-bar blues with one riff and a few bars of your own.

notes: Next step, not now: Tim Richards, Improvising Blues Piano (Schott) assumes about Grade 3, roughly a year of steady practice. Keep it for year 2.

modules.title: Jazz
modules.intro: Works best after month 5, once you have seventh chords. Swaps into the technique and repertoire blocks; warm-up, reading and theory follow the main plan.

technique.text: Shell voicings (root + 3rd + 7th) for ii–V–I in C: Dm7–G7–Cmaj7, left hand.

repertoire.text: “Autumn Leaves” from a lead sheet: melody in the right hand, shells in the left, first 8 bars.

weeks.doneWhen: ii–V–I in C with shells, both hands, slowly.

technique.text: Shell voicings for ii–V–I in F and B♭.

repertoire.text: Autumn Leaves: the A sections, melody + shells.

weeks.doneWhen: ii–V–I shells in C, F and B♭ without stopping.

technique.text: Chord-scale basics: Dorian over m7, Mixolydian over dom7. Play each scale over its shell.

repertoire.text: Autumn Leaves: the whole form, melody + shells, slowly.

weeks.doneWhen: Autumn Leaves, whole form, without stopping.

technique.text: Reading jazz chord symbols on a lead sheet: a shell for every chord in Autumn Leaves.

repertoire.text: Autumn Leaves recorded, plus a few bars of improvisation with the chord scales.

weeks.doneWhen: A recorded Autumn Leaves with shells in the left hand.

notes: Book: Tim Richards, Beginning Jazz Piano, Part 1 (Schott; also a MusicGurus video course). His Exploring Jazz Piano vol. 1 suits Grade 4 and above, so it comes later.
